notes: Bratska Mogila (1956): a 41 m tapering grey granite obelisk with a red-star emblem; in front of its foot stands a bronze male and female partisan pair (about 4–5 m) on a stepped plinth, flanked left and right by two low granite walls (each about 10 m long, about 4 m high) carrying high-relief bronze crowds. The figure and wall sizes are estimates from photos.
One of two eternal-flame bowls at Bratska Mogila. OSM gives a round footprint about 2.5 m across. The height of about 1 m is a guess, because no photo of the bowls was found.
The second eternal-flame bowl at Bratska Mogila, about 50 m south-west of the first one. OSM gives a round footprint about 2.5 m across. The height is a guess.

Kambanite (1979): a central 37 m tower of four tall grey concrete slab-pylons joined at the top by an open ring or sphere that holds bells. Around it is a roughly 66 m circular complex (the OSM outline) of low concrete walls and benches with over 100 donated bells. The tower footprint is an estimate from photos.

Patriarch Evtimiy at the Popa square (Marko Markov, 1938–39): a bronze patriarch in a long robe and cowl, holding a cross before his chest. The polished dark granite pedestal is an inverted truncated pyramid on a two-step platform.

Unknown Soldier (1981), against the south wall of the St Sofia basilica: a low grey granite wall-sarcophagus bearing Vazov's verse and bronze wreaths, a low granite altar and a dark bronze eternal-flame ring in front, and seven flag pylons on one side. Andrey Nikolov's bronze lying lion (about 4 m long) sits on a low plinth a little in front. The wall size is an estimate from photos.

Doctors' Monument (1884): a 10 m four-sided truncated pyramid of large rough-faced white sandstone blocks carved with names, on a grey granite plinth and topped by a monolithic grey granite sarcophagus. Eight bronze wreaths hang on the base. The base is 10 × 8 m. Its main face is described as oriented west.

Odrin Epic monument: a tapering pyramidal obelisk of grey Vladaya granite on a 7 × 7 m stepped base, crowned by a 2.8 m white Vratsa-stone militiaman in a greatcoat holding a rifle. A bronze medallion with a laurel wreath and a bronze battle relief are on the front, which faces east. The total height is 12 m.

Aviation monument (2012): a 10.6 m dark-grey granite-clad concrete shaft with an asymmetrically narrowing rectangular section, topped by a 1.5 m brass eagle with a 2.5 m wingspan. At its foot stand two light travertine curved 'wing' slabs (4.3 m and 3 m high, 4.3 m and 3.8 m long, 0.4 m thick) on a 13 × 13 m square platform with a marble propeller inlay.

Memorial to the victims of the communist regime (1999): a 58 m wall in polished black granite, in angled sections, inscribed with 7,526 names. In front stands an old carved light-stone Christian cross (about 1.8 m), and a small chapel is part of the complex. The wall height of about 3 m is estimated from photos.

This is NOT the main monument. It is one of two secondary bronze sculpture groups (soldiers and civilians, with a cart or gun wheel) still standing on grey granite plinths beside the approach to the former Monument to the Soviet Army from Tsar Osvoboditel Blvd; this one is on the north-west side. A July 2026 photo shows both groups in place. The main pylon about 130 m south-west has lost its three top figures (cut down in December 2023) and its bas-reliefs (in storage at Lozen); scaffolding was removed in 2026 and the bare grey stone shaft, about 25–29 m by estimate, still stands. The sizes here are estimates from the OSM outline (5.7 × 1.9 m) and the photo, which suggests the plinth may be up to about 8 m wide.

The second secondary bronze group (soldiers and partisans with a flag) on a grey granite plinth, south-east of the approach to the partially dismantled Soviet Army monument, mirroring w1217586052. It was still standing in July 2026. The bas-reliefs and top figures of the main pylon have been removed; the bare pylon shaft remains about 130 m south-west.

Monument to the revolutionaries of Macedonia and Adrianople (2016): two 5 m stylised white-stone wings rising side by side like flames or feathers, carved with 150 names, on a low faceted light-stone base inscribed 'Българийо, за тебе...'. The base size is an estimate; the paved plaza is about 17 m square.

'Mother' (Serdika – Mayka, Velichko Minekov, 1976) in front of Sofia Central Station: a tall angular, faceted light-grey concrete or stone pylon that zig-zags upward, with a dark seated mother holding children attached about a third of the way up. The height of about 18 m is an estimate from photos.

Flat granite floor plaques and stars: nothing stands up, so no model. Bulgarian Alley of Glory (2005) in front of the Arena Mladost cinema: flat granite floor plaques, some replaced by gold stars with signatures. There is nothing vertical, so it is best rendered flush with the ground or skipped.

Stefan Stambolov (1995): a giant dark bronze head split by a vertical cleft, standing on a dark granite block that rises from a broken, tilted granite slab with his signature, in Crystal Garden. The sizes are estimates from photos.

St Kliment Ohridski (Lyubomir Dalchev, 1978–79), opposite Sofia University: a tall, columnar, stylised robed saint in light stone with both arms raised, holding a metal torch in each hand, on a plain square light-granite plinth on a polygonal platform. The sizes are estimates from photos.

Ivan Vazov (by St Sofia, Rakovski St): a dark bronze figure seated on a rock with a book in his right hand, on a light-stone block pedestal on a low stepped platform. The sizes are estimates from photos.

Tsar Samuil (2014): a 3.7 m bronze crowned ruler in long robes and cloak, holding a tall patriarchal-cross sceptre in his right hand and a sheathed sword at his left side, on a 2 m light-stone pedestal. He faces the Samuil's Warriors group to the south-south-west.

'Samuil's Warriors' by Lyubomir Dalchev (1970s design): a bronze group of blinded Bulgarian soldiers placed facing the 2014 Tsar Samuil statue. The figure count and sizes were not found in sources and are guesses.

Sts Cyril and Methodius (Vladimir Ginovski, 1975) in front of the National Library: two 4.2 m robed monks standing shoulder to shoulder and holding an unrolled scroll with the alphabet between them, on a tall light granite block inscribed 'Кирил и Методий'. The photos show green-patinated bronze, though Bulgarian Wikipedia says stone. The pedestal height is estimated.

Paisiy Hilendarski (Mihail Simeonov, 1965): an elongated, expressive bronze monk in a long habit raising one arm high (holding a quill or scroll), on a rough-hewn stone block. It faces St Alexander Nevsky Cathedral. The sizes are estimates from photos.

'The Bulgarian Volunteer' (2008): a bronze opalchenets with a flag (after Veshin's 'Samara Flag') on a tall rectangular dark granite pedestal with bronze reliefs on all four sides, on a stepped platform shaped like the 'Cross for Bravery' order seen from above. The total height is 7 m.

Aleksandar Stamboliyski, in front of the National Opera on Rakovski St: a larger-than-life dark bronze standing figure in a long open coat, on a low granite plinth. The sizes are estimates from photos.

St George fountain (Mina Ivanov, 1935, restored): a small bronze St George on a rearing horse spearing the dragon, on a round granite column-fountain standing in a round granite basin about 3 m across, in front of the St Sofia church. The sizes are estimates from photos.

Monument of the Soviet Soldier in Lozenets (near Hotel Hemus): a dark bronze Red Army soldier in a cape with a submachine gun across his chest, standing on a heap of captured banners, on a light-grey granite block with wreath reliefs and steps, backed by a long low relief wall. The sizes are estimates from a 2005 photo, and its 2026 status was not separately confirmed.

A second statue of Patriarch Evtimiy near Cherni Vrah Blvd and James Bourchier (St Mina garden). No source or photo was found, so only the OSM tags are known; render it as a generic robed figure on a plinth.

'Opalchenets and Russian soldier' (Ivan Blazhev, 1953): a light-grey stone two-figure group (a Bulgarian volunteer with a rifle and a Russian soldier embracing his shoulder) on a granite block. It is one of four corner groups of the 'Most na druzhbata' bridge and is NOT part of the Soviet Army monument. The sizes are estimates from photos.

'Soviet specialist and Bulgarian technician' (Iliya Iliev, 1953): a light-grey stone two-figure civilian group (the taller Russian embraces the Bulgarian holding a scroll) on a granite block at a corner of the 'Most na druzhbata' bridge. The sizes are estimates from photos.

'Partisan and Soviet soldier' (Stefan Stoimirov, 1953): a light-grey stone two-figure group (a partisan with a submachine gun and a Red Army soldier holding flowers) on a granite block at a corner of the 'Most na druzhbata' bridge. The sizes are estimates from photos.

Georgi S. Rakovski (Lilyana Marinova, 1967) in front of the Rakovski Military Academy: a bronze standing figure in a long coat with one hand resting on a sabre, on a plain granite block on a low base. The sizes are estimates from photos.

Giuseppe Garibaldi (Georgi Chapkanov, 2010): a small dark bronze Garibaldi with a raised sabre on a horse rearing on its hind legs (the sculpture is 2 m tall, 130 kg), set on a high, slender round granite column. The column height is estimated from photos.

Taras Shevchenko (Igor Grechanik, 2009/2016): a 4 m dark bronze young Shevchenko holding his 'Kobzar' book, engulfed by tall curling flame-like forms that arch over his head and rise from a tree-root base, on a low red-granite plinth.

Georgi Asparuhov – Gundi (Lyubomir Grigorov, 2023): a 2.5 m polished brown bronze footballer dribbling a ball, standing on a small artificial mound fronted by a long, low curved light-grey marble wall with a bronze plaque (the OSM outline is 16 × 5 m).

Atanas Burov (Emil Popov, 2011) in the City Garden: a life-size-plus dark bronze figure in a long coat, standing on a large square, 20 cm high, dark polished stone plinth reached by concrete steps. The figure height is estimated.

'Maykata' (The Mother) in the City Garden by the National Theatre: a weathered grey-brown carved tree trunk showing a woman's head and torso with a child's face carved lower down. Identified from a geotagged Commons photo 4 m from the node; the photo date and current condition are unknown.

'Sundial' sculpture (mapped in 2025) in a round plaza about 11 m across, per the OSM outline. No description or photo was found; render a flat dial disc with a slanted gnomon of about 2.5 m (a guess).
Monument to the fighter pilots (2007): an upright polished black granite slab (3.5 m) inscribed with names, topped by a light-grey eagle with spread wings, on a small base.

Ivan Vazov's grave (1926) behind the St Sofia church: a large rough grey granite boulder inscribed 'Иванъ Вазовъ 1850-1921', at the head of a flower-bed grave plot with a stone kerb. The size is estimated from photos.

name: Паметник на Съветската армия
notes: Monument to the Soviet Army (1954). The three top figures were removed in December 2023 and the bas-reliefs too; the bare stone shaft (about 25-29 m, an estimate from 2026 photos) still stands on its stepped plaza. Mapped as was:historic=monument.
